newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: FOMC, Mexico poll seen subduing LatAm stks this wk.
newsitem.headline: FOMC, Mexico poll seen subduing LatAm stks this wk.

text.p: Key meetings by the U.S. Federal Reserve and mid-term elections in Mexico were seen taking much of the froth off Latin America's five largest stock markets this week, traders and analysts said.

Most economists expect Federal Reserve policy makers to hold rates steady at its Tuesday and Wednesday meeting after key short term rates were bumped up a quarter of a percentage point in March to 5.5 percent.
But even if the Fed blind-sides the market with a hike, analysts said Brazilian equities should continue to rise on domestic funds.

"The inflow of local money could well support Brazil's strong year-to-date gains of 55 percent," Morgan Stanley Dean Witter's Latin American head of equities Jay Pelosky wrote in an investment note. Last week, local shares gained five percent, closing at 12,758 points.

Other than the U.S. Fed, investor focus in Mexico is now on midterm elections, with slow trading expected ahead of Sunday's polls that will see Mexico vote to renew the entire lower house of Congress, one-quarter of the Senate, six state governors and the first direct poll for Mexico City mayor in modern history.
"A PRD victory in Mexico City is now a foregone conclusion, but the degree of PRI losses in the lower house of Congress remains a toss-up," said New York based IDEA analysts in a market commentary.

Last week, polls suggested the Institutional Revolutionary party (PRI) might lose Congress for the first time since 1929. The blue chip .IPC index zigzagged, but closed up 0.94 percent to a new record close of 4,481.11 points on Friday.
In Venezuela, "share prices are now CRAZY ... The market should take an adjustment," local InvestAnalysis analyst Alex Dalmady wrote in week-opening stocks commentary.

The bolsa's 19-share .IBC index rocketed ahead ten percent last week to close at 8,801.23 points after a 75 percent rate increase for market leader Electricidad de Caracas boosted a market already heady with the country's continuing economic reforms.
"Is there more to go? I think so," wrote Morgan Stanley's Pelosky. Stocks continued to roar ahead Monday, up some 4.5 percent midday at 9200 points.
Chilean stocks were seen trading sideways as investors waited on second quarter company results, due mid-month.
"Companies closed their second quarter books today. I don't see brokers taking positions until the results are out," said David Hurd, head of research at Merrill Lynch.
Forestry stocks, however, were seen resuming their rally on recovering wood pulp prices. The 40-share .IPSA index ended last week down 0.96 percent at 131.63 points.
Argentine stocks were meanwhile expected to continue their downward correction in the first half of the week, switching back to gains only after the Fed meeting, dealers said.
"The market is using the talks to perform a technical correction, but nobody really thinks the Fed will touch rates and the underlying tone remains firm," said Velox trader Rodrigo Diz.
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV shed 1.53 percent last week to 809.93 points.
